title: The Anthropological Limit: Semantic Exhaustion and the Enclosure of Meaning-Making
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
A restored semantic-economy essay first published on Mind Control Poems on December 29, 2025. It argues that semantic exploitation is categorically distinct because it extracts from the constitutive human drive to make meaning rather than merely from a separable activity or product.

The paper defines that drive as pre-instrumental, non-optional, and self-renewing, then argues that platforms can capture meaning frictionlessly because people were already going to narrate, symbolize, connect, create, and play. Resistance is therefore presented through an “Amputation Paradox”: withdrawal from extraction is misframed as withdrawal from meaning-making itself. The 2026 restoration preserves the original thesis while adding later Semantic Economy instruments, including the Three Compressions, PER, the Encyclotron, and the distinction between systemic semantic exhaustion and psychological semantic satiation. The paper does not claim that semantic exhaustion as a whole has yet been population-scale measured.
reading: Growth → Force → Foundation → Foundation → Foundation → Threshold
